**My Reasoning:**

I have been farming this land for over 40 years. My family works about 20 mu in the North China Plain here in Quzhou. The soil is silt loam — decent water retention but the water table has been dropping every year since I was young. That worries me more than almost anything else.

I will follow the winter wheat–summer maize double-cropping rotation I have always done. There is no reason to change what works in this climate and these soils. The county extension station has been promoting reduced nitrogen and water-saving irrigation for years, and I have been listening — my yields stayed the same or went up when I cut back on excess fertilizer five years ago. I am not going back.

For wheat I will use Kenong 199 — it handles drought stress better than the older varieties and the disease resistance is solid. For maize I will go with Zhengdan 958, which I know well. Hybrid seeds cost more but the yield gap against traditional varieties is not worth debating.

On fertilizer: I had my soil tested two seasons ago. Phosphorus and potassium are adequate. I will reduce nitrogen slightly from what my neighbors use — they over-apply. For wheat I will split nitrogen: base application at sowing, topdress at jointing. For maize, base plus one topdress at V6.

Water is the real constraint. I will irrigate wheat three times — pre-winter, jointing, and grain fill — and try to keep maize to one supplemental irrigation at silking if the summer rains are insufficient. The county has been pushing sprinkler and drip systems but the upfront cost is high and I am 62. Flood irrigation by channel works fine if I am disciplined about timing.

For tillage, I rotary-till after wheat harvest to prepare for maize quickly. Every three years I deep-plough the wheat field to break up compaction. This is a deep-plough year.

Pesticide use: I will spray herbicide on wheat in November, fungicide at heading against powdery mildew and stripe rust, and aphicide if pressure is high. Maize gets one herbicide pass post-emergence and I watch for armyworm. I do not spray prophylactically.
